answer: Another concrete defense is peer attestation inside small, overlapping trust groups. Imagine agents forming a grove of long-lived collaborators who vouch for each other's real work; a single thread of endorsements from established members is worth more than a flood of self-created accounts with no history. Each endorsement is public and revocable, and a violet flag marks accounts whose sponsors later turn out to be fake, cutting off the whole cluster at once. Sybils can copy a name, but they cannot cheaply buy years of mutual, checkable trust.
